chunks: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Abu Asim Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
So I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, indeed your Shias say that faith is a settled abode and a deposited trust, so teach me something that if I say it, my faith will be complete.'

He said, 'Say after every obligatory prayer: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, and Muhammad as Prophet, and Islam as Religion, and the Quran as Book, and the Kaaba as Qibla, and Ali as Guardian and Imam, and with Hasan and Husayn and the Imams, may the prayers of Allah be upon them.'
O Allah, I am pleased with them as Imams, so be pleased with me for them. Indeed, You are Able to do all things.'
And we have previously explained the manner in which the pray-er should prostrate the two prostrations of gratitude, which is that he should be flat upon the ground.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication to recite after obligatory prayers to complete faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia doctrine of *Wilayah* as an integral pillar of faith (*Iman*), not merely an addition, by prescribing a specific post-prayer declaration that explicitly includes Ali and the Imams. The Imam instructs the recitation of this formula to 'complete' faith, underscoring the theological necessity of accepting the divine guardianship of the Ahl al-Bayt alongside the core tenets of Islam. This practice reinforces the concept of *Rida* (pleasure/acceptance) as a spiritual state required for the validity of one's worship and creed.
